payload.rationale: No forecast or observational evidence was supplied, so this estimate rests on climatology for Miami (MIA) in mid/late September. Normal daily high is roughly 88-89°F, with typical daily variability of about ±2-3°F: convective/rainy days often cap highs near 84-87°F, while drier, sunnier days commonly reach 90-92°F. Recent years have skewed warm, with September highs of 90-91°F very common. Treating the target band 88-89°F as covering 87.5-89.5°F on a distribution centered near 89-89.5°F with SD ~2.5°F gives roughly 25-32% probability. This band sits near the center of the distribution, so it is one of the more likely two-degree bins, but the mass is spread across roughly 85-93°F. Too high: recent-year warmth and a dry mid-September pattern could push the mode to 90-91°F, leaving 88-89 as a below-mode bin; also settlement uses The Weather Company's reported value, which may differ from NWS observations. Too low: if a wetter or cloudier pattern dominates (possible late in the wet season or with tropical moisture), highs could cluster at 88-89°F, and a two-degree bin at the climatological center can capture 35%+ of outcomes in some years. Given complete absence of current forecast data, I stay close to the climatological base rate.
limitations: No forecast, observed, or synoptic data supplied for the date.
Climatological distribution estimated from general knowledge, not computed from records.
Settlement source (The Weather Company for CLIMIA) may differ slightly from NWS station values.
Possible rounding/preliminary-vs-final data issues in settlement.
